description: Canonical, machine-readable trust profile for apohara-sealchain (apohara-seal-v1). Single source of truth for: what each layer and combination proves (matrix), the named attestation profiles the policy engine and the transparency dashboard consume (profiles), and the qualified-TSA host allowlist. The human-readable rendering is docs/TRUST-PROFILE.md, which cross-references this file. The crate embeds an identical copy (crates/apohara-sealchain-core/trust-profile.json) via include_str!; a dev-only test asserts the two stay byte-identical.

layers.hmac: Has this receipt's preimage been altered, given the shared secret?
layers.ed25519: Did the holder of this private key author this seal?
layers.tsa: Did this content exist before a point in time, according to that TSA?
layers.rekor: Is this seal publicly recorded in an append-only transparency log?
layers.c2pa: Is there a provenance manifest bound to this payload?

offline-basic.title: Offline basic
offline-basic.description: Local integrity + authorship + provenance, fully offline. The default seal.

transparency.title: Public transparency
transparency.description: Authorship plus a public, append-only Sigstore Rekor v2 transparency-log record.

legal-grade.title: Legal-grade timestamp
legal-grade.description: Authorship plus a qualified eIDAS QTSP timestamp (legal weight under eIDAS Art. 42). Requires pointing --tsa at a QTSP you are authorised to use; the default TSA is NOT qualified.

full.title: Full five-layer
full.description: Every layer present and independently re-verified: integrity + authorship + timestamp + public transparency + provenance.

matrix.proves: Local integrity: anyone holding the shared secret can confirm the receipt's preimage is unmodified.
matrix.doesNotProve: Authorship (anyone with the secret can forge it), existence-in-time, public record, provenance.
matrix.trustAnchor: The shared HMAC secret (symmetric; the verifier must already hold it).

matrix.proves: Authorship by the key holder: the seal was signed by whoever controls that Ed25519 private key. The public key is embedded, so verification is offline.
matrix.doesNotProve: Who that key holder is (no identity/PKI binding), when it was signed, public record, provenance.
matrix.trustAnchor: The Ed25519 keypair (plus out-of-band trust that the embedded public key is really the claimed author's).

matrix.proves: Existence-before-a-point-in-time as asserted by a non-qualified TSA (e.g. FreeTSA/Sigstore): the hmac.sig||ed25519.sig binding was timestamped and the imprint is re-checked offline.
matrix.doesNotProve: A legally-qualified/court-admissible timestamp; identity; public record; provenance. A free TSA is credible but not eIDAS-qualified.
matrix.trustAnchor: The TSA's signing certificate (imprint is the pass bar; chain validation is best-effort: 'Valid, not Trusted').

matrix.proves: A qualified timestamp: existence-before-time with legal effect under eIDAS Art. 42, recognised across the EU. Same offline imprint check; the legal weight comes from the QTSP.
matrix.doesNotProve: Authorship identity beyond the Ed25519 key, public record, provenance. It does not turn an unqualified key into a qualified signature.
matrix.trustAnchor: A qualified eIDAS TSA under your own QTSP account. GATED: needs your credentials.

matrix.proves: Public, append-only record: a DSSE-signed in-toto Statement anchoring the canonical preimage was admitted to a Sigstore Rekor v2 log, with an offline-verifiable inclusion proof + signed checkpoint.
matrix.doesNotProve: Legal qualification, identity (the DSSE is signed by the seal key, not an OIDC identity), provenance. Transparency is not qualification.
matrix.trustAnchor: The Rekor log's public key, pinned with provenance in packaging/rekor-shards.json (verified offline).

matrix.proves: A provenance manifest is cryptographically bound to the payload (sidecar JUMBF, or in-file hard binding with --embed): tooling can show the claimed origin/history.
matrix.doesNotProve: A third-party-trust-anchored credential: in v0.1 the manifest is self-signed with the seal's Ed25519 key (trust check disabled: 'Valid, not Trusted'). Not legal qualification, not identity.
matrix.trustAnchor: A real C2PA Signer certificate for production provenance (v0.1 uses a self-signed cert).

matrix.proves: The union of all of the above, produced real-or-abort under --all: integrity + authorship + timestamp + public transparency + provenance, each independently re-checked at verify time.
matrix.doesNotProve: Anything no single layer proves: notably legal-grade timestamping unless the TSA is a qualified eIDAS QTSP, and third-party identity binding. --all uses the default (non-qualified) TSA.
matrix.trustAnchor: All anchors above; for legal weight you must additionally point --tsa at an eIDAS QTSP.

qualifiedTsaHonesty: knownQualifiedTsaHosts is a NON-EXHAUSTIVE convenience allowlist of TSA hostnames operated by providers that appear on EU Trusted Lists as qualified trust service providers offering qualified timestamping. Matching it proves only that a receipt's recorded TSA authority host is on this list; it does NOT cryptographically prove the eIDAS qualification of any individual token. The authoritative source is the EU Trusted List. Operators should extend this for their own QTSP via a policy's require_tsa_authority_in, which overrides this allowlist.
